next_page.text: Maya took out her plate and glass, and walked to the lunch line. She watched her classmates gathering into their groups, talking, laughing and playing. Once when she had joined them, they had made fun of her dark skin and her curly hair. She had felt hurt. Now, she stood alone at the end of the line, waiting her turn.

speech.utterance: I'll just wait my turn at the end of the line.
speech.speaker: Maya

text.text: Maya stood quietly at the end of the lunch line, clutching her plate and glass tightly. All around her, children laughed and shouted, forming happy little circles on the ground. She lowered her head, remembering the mean words from yesterday. "Why does no one ever save a seat for me?" she whispered to herself.

Maya stood alone at the back of the line, her linger hot but lips tight. She remembered how Rosy Miss used to whisper, then how they ganged on her. "My friends play games now," Maya thought. "But Maya is different."

Maya's eyes welled up as she stood at the end of the line, her plate and glass in hand. She remembered the past teasing she had faced, and a tear rolled down her cheek. The laughter and chatter of her classmates filled the air, but she felt isolated and alone.
Classmates gather in groups, laughing and chatting as they wait for lunch. "We're all in this together."

Maya stood at the end of the line. She stood alone and had of her plate. The children remembered her laughter and had called her. "I wonder if the person gets me alone when I am holding her plate,” she said to herself. Yes. laughter! She had teased her with games. laughter, laughter. She walked, playing with her plate. called the bell. The bell rang. it was her turn.
